commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Gwendlyn Di Corci ({U}{B}{B}{R} 3/5 legendary Human Rogue; Legends 1994-06-01, reprinted in Masters Edition III 2009-09-07; Reserved List; commander-legal, not a Game Changer, no project exception). '{T}: Target player discards a card at random. Activate only during your turn.' Plan (owner blueprint 2026-10-14): make Gwendlyn a repeatable random-discard engine with haste (Lightning Greaves, Thousand-Year Elixir), untaps (Pemmin's Aura, Minamo, Magewright's Stone, Patriar's Seal, Elixir) and copies (Illusionist's Bracers). Refill opposing hands with wheels and strip them again. Convert discards into cards, mana, stolen permanents and life loss (Waste Not, Geth's Grimoire, Liliana's Caress, the three Tinybones, Tergrid, Sheoldred, Bowmasters, Bloodchief Ascension). Candidate: Hymn to Tourach replaces Dauthi Voidwalker, whose exile replacement stopped Tergrid, Tinybones, Bauble Burglar and Bloodchief Ascension.
protected_core: Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lantern
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 (Optimized), unchanged. Game Changers: 17 in both baseline and candidate (Ancient Tomb, Chrome Mox, Cyclonic Rift, Demonic Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Force of Will, Gamble, Imperial Seal, Lion's Eye Diamond, Mystical Tutor, Notion Thief, Opposition Agent, Orcish Bowmasters, Rhystic Study, Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lantern, Underworld Breach, Vampiric Tutor). Commander Spellbook find-my-combos: 1 -> 1 complete combo (1368-2706-3518 Underworld Breach + Lion's Eye Diamond + Wheel of Fortune); almost-included 52 -> 50. The owner rejected generic combo conversion (Mindcrank + Bloodchief Ascension) and a Thoracle/Breach turbo shell, so the Aphetto + Bracers infinite (283-4091) is not adopted without the owner.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Commander-first to Gwendlyn's Oracle: the add is random discard in the commander's own idiom, and the cut restores the graveyard payoffs the owner kept. Distinctness (nonbasic names shared with the most similar approved Grixis decks, baseline -> candidate, canonical Archidekt exports): Crosis, the Purger 55 -> 56 (Crosis also runs Hymn to Tourach); Nekusar, the Mindrazer 54 -> 54; Lord Xander, the Collector 50 -> 50; Nicol Bolas 46 -> 46; The Madcap Jester 45 -> 44; Grixistax October 2026 45 -> 44. Dauthi Voidwalker appears in seven other Grixis decks, so cutting it here also reduces homogenization. Nekusar is the nearest wheel deck. This list stays commander-first on Gwendlyn's own tap-to-discard Oracle (untap/copy package), not draw punishment. Owner-removed or rejected cards and classes (Megrim, Counterspell, Burning Inquiry, Winds of Change, The Locust God, Bone Miser, Fell Specter, Hypnotic Specter, Sangromancer, Feed the Swarm, Aphetto Alchemist, Battlemage's Bracers, Freed from the Real, Liliana of the Veil, Syphon Mind, Unnerve, Necrogen Mists, Naktamun Lorespinner, Quest for the Nihil Stone, Raiders' Wake, Painful Quandary, Cao Cao, Lord of Wei, Monument to Endurance, Mindcrank, Mox Diamond, generic Thoracle/Breach turbo-combo) are not re-added.

U/B/R sources (fetches and rainbow lands counted per colour) are 21/24/17. 64 nonland cards; curve MV0 3, MV1 12, MV2 20, MV3 22, MV4 4, MV5 3 (identical: Dauthi and Hymn are both MV2); average nonland MV 2.328. Creatures 14 -> 13. Exact enumeration of paid {U}{B}{B}{R}: play T3 0.1439, play T4 0.5110, draw T4 0.6035 in both lists. The colour-agnostic upper bound is play T4 0.555 (only 4.4 points higher), so no manabase swap is indicated. Sulfurous Springs over Crumbling Necropolis: 0.5094.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Force of Will, Force of Negation, Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Swan Song, Deflecting Swat, An Offer You Can't Refuse. Dauthi's continuous exile was the deck's second graveyard answer, which is a disclosed loss against opposing Breach/reanimator decks. Commander protection: Lightning Greaves, Pemmin's Aura shroud (optional), Deflecting Swat.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Gwendlyn Di Corci general 48/380 (synergy 0.124), upgraded 5/26 (synergy 0.19), optimized 5/31 (synergy 0.159), cEDH absent; live Scryfall batch
material_candidates.role: {B}{B} sorcery: target player discards two cards at random.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Dauthi Voidwalker ({B}{B} 3/2 shadow; replaces opponents' cards going to a graveyard with exile plus a void counter; sacrifice to play one void card free). Dauthi is not in the owner's explicit retained-challenged list, but the owner's blueprint names it under 'resource denial/value asymmetry'. Cutting it is therefore a FLAGGED override, made on rules evidence. Its replacement stops three cards the owner explicitly kept: Tergrid, God of Fright must put the card 'from a graveyard' (ruling 2021-02-05: it fails if the card left the graveyard); Tinybones, Bauble Burglar must 'exile it from their graveyard'; and Bloodchief Ascension's payoff needs a card 'put into an opponent's graveyard'. Discard-trigger payoffs (Liliana's Caress, Waste Not, Geth's Grimoire, Tourach, Tinybones, Trinket Thief) still work under Dauthi (ruling 2021-06-18). Also lost: continuous graveyard hate against opposing Breach/reanimator decks (only Bojuka Bog remains), a 3-power shadow clock, and one free opposing card.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: The same {B}{B} becomes two more random discards, mirroring Gwendlyn's Oracle as Mind Twist does (the owner accepted Mind Twist as 'efficient, scalable random discard that directly mirrors the commander's defining mechanic'). With Dauthi gone, every discarded or sacrificed card reaches the graveyard, so Tergrid, Tinybones, Bauble Burglar and Bloodchief Ascension work again. In the bounded ledger, one turn with one Gwendlyn activation goes from 1 discard to 3; Caress life loss 2 -> 6; Waste Not triggers 1 -> 3; Burglar stash 0 -> 3; Ascension drains 0 -> 6 life; expected Tergrid steals vs a 7-card hand with 3 permanents 0 -> 9/7.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: One-shot: dead against empty hands, where Dauthi still attacks and still hates graveyards. The owner rejected Syphon Mind, Unnerve and Necrogen Mists as 'generic redundancy'. Hymn differs because it is random, 2 MV and one-target like Mind Twist, but that distinction is a judgment call and is disclosed. Loses continuous graveyard hate.
material_candidates.reason: The cut is high-confidence rules evidence: Dauthi switches off three owner-kept engines. Hymn is the best in-class random-discard filler for the same {B}{B}. One genuine swap; not enough for the five-swap floor.
